intro: This search tracks retail space listed for lease across Palm Beach, Broward and Miami-Dade counties: in-line shop space in neighborhood and grocery-anchored centers, end caps, second-generation restaurant space, and free-standing pad sites.

Retail availability in South Florida is tight, so well-located space often leases quickly. Bill works on the tenant side: shortlisting spaces that fit your trade area and frontage needs, comparing asking rents and total occupancy costs (base rent plus taxes, insurance and common-area charges), and negotiating terms such as free rent, tenant-improvement allowances and renewal options.
Each week the search is re-run and the page shows how many spaces are available, what changed, and a link to every active listing with photos and full details.
faqs: Who pays the broker when I lease retail space?
In most commercial leases the landlord pays the leasing commissions, including the tenant's broker. Bill confirms how the commission is handled on each space before you sign anything.
What does NNN mean on a retail lease?

On a triple-net (NNN) lease the tenant pays base rent plus a share of the property's taxes, insurance and common-area maintenance. Ask for the current NNN estimate on every space so you can compare total occupancy cost, not just base rent.
Can I lease a second-generation restaurant space?
Yes. Spaces that already have a hood, grease trap and plumbing can save significant build-out cost and time. Tell Bill your kitchen needs and he will flag the spaces that fit.

intro: This search tracks office space listed for lease across Palm Beach, Broward and Miami-Dade: Class A towers, suburban office parks, and smaller professional buildings with suites for law, accounting, financial and creative firms.

The office market here is split. The newest, best-located buildings lease up fast, while older buildings often offer meaningful concessions. Bill helps tenants compare full-service and net quotes on an equal basis, weigh parking and commute, and negotiate concessions such as free rent and improvement allowances.
The page is refreshed weekly with the number of available spaces, a short note on what changed, and a link to every active listing.
faqs: What is the difference between a full-service and a net office lease?

A full-service (gross) rent includes most operating costs such as taxes, insurance, maintenance and often utilities and janitorial. A net rent adds some or all of those on top. Comparing spaces fairly means converting every quote to the same basis.
How long are typical office lease terms?
Terms of three to five years are common for small and mid-size suites, with longer terms usually earning larger concessions. Short-term and executive-suite options exist for flexibility.
Who pays my tenant-representation broker?
In most office leases the landlord pays the leasing commissions, including the tenant's broker. Bill confirms the arrangement on each space before you commit.

intro: This search tracks retail investment property for sale across South Florida: neighborhood strip centers, multi-tenant retail buildings, and free-standing retail, priced from $750,000.

Retail has been one of the region's strongest property types, with grocery-anchored and service tenants leading demand. Bill helps investors review rent rolls, lease terms and tenant quality, and compare pricing across listings.

faqs: What makes a strip center a stronger investment?
Look at tenant mix and credit, remaining lease terms, how expenses are recovered from tenants, traffic and visibility, and whether an anchor such as a grocer drives daily visits.
What is a cap rate?

The capitalization rate is the property's net operating income divided by its price. It lets you compare the income return of properties at different prices, but it should always be checked against a verified rent roll and expenses.
Can I use a 1031 exchange to buy retail property?

Investment real estate can often be acquired through a 1031 exchange. The rules and deadlines are strict, so work with a qualified intermediary and your tax adviser; Bill can coordinate the property side.

faqs: Should my business buy or lease its warehouse?

Owning builds equity and fixes your occupancy cost, while leasing keeps capital free and adds flexibility. Many owner-users buy through a separate entity and lease the building to their operating company.
What due diligence matters most on industrial property?
Zoning and permitted uses, environmental history (a Phase I report), roof and structure condition, loading and clear height, and flood zone.
Is SBA financing available for owner-occupied industrial?
Owner-occupied commercial property can often qualify for SBA 504 or 7(a) financing. A lender can confirm eligibility; Bill can introduce you to lenders who do these loans.

faqs: Is buying an office building a good fit for my practice or firm?

faqs: Should my practice buy its own office?

Owning gives control over the space and turns rent into equity, and many practices hold the property in a separate entity that leases to the practice. Compare it with a long-term lease, and involve your accountant.
What is a medical office condo?
It is an individually owned unit within a medical building, with shared common areas managed by an association. It lets smaller practices own without buying a whole building.
What makes medical office different from regular office?
Plumbing in exam rooms, higher parking needs, ADA requirements, zoning for medical use and proximity to hospitals and referral sources all affect value and usability.

faqs: How is mixed-use property financed?

Diversified income from different tenant types, often in walkable, high-demand locations, and sometimes favorable zoning for redevelopment.
What risks should I watch for?
Different lease structures for each use, higher insurance complexity, and the effect of a commercial vacancy on total income.

intro: This search tracks triple-net (NNN) leased investment property for sale: single-tenant retail, restaurant, medical and service buildings where the tenant pays the property's taxes, insurance and maintenance in addition to rent.

NNN property is popular with investors who want predictable income and light management, including buyers completing 1031 exchanges. Value depends on tenant credit, remaining lease term, rent increases and the real estate underneath. Bill helps buyers compare those factors across listings.
The search is refreshed weekly with the current count and a link to every active listing.
faqs: What does triple-net (NNN) mean?

The tenant pays the property's real estate taxes, insurance and maintenance on top of base rent, so the owner's income is closer to the rent itself. Some leases leave roof or structure with the landlord, so read each lease.
What should I look at first on a NNN listing?
Tenant credit and guarantor, years remaining on the lease, rent increases, renewal options, and whether the location would re-lease well if the tenant left.
Are NNN properties good for a 1031 exchange?
They are a common choice because they are easy to identify and manage. Exchange rules and deadlines are strict, so use a qualified intermediary and your tax adviser.

faqs: How are apartment buildings valued?
Mainly on net operating income: rents less operating expenses, divided by a market cap rate. Price per unit and comparable sales are useful cross-checks.

A current rent roll, trailing 12-month income and expense statement, leases, utility bills, insurance and tax bills, and any recent inspection or recertification reports.
Do buildings in Florida have special inspection rules?

Florida has milestone inspection and reserve requirements for certain condominium and cooperative buildings, and local recertification rules for older buildings. Confirm what applies to the building you are buying.

Short-term rental rules vary city by city in South Florida, from registration and inspections to minimum-stay limits, and condo and homeowner associations often add their own restrictions. Bill helps investors confirm the rules for each property before they rely on nightly-rental income.
Each week the search is re-run, and this page shows the count and a link to every active listing.
faqs: Are short-term rentals allowed everywhere in South Florida?

No. Many cities require registration, inspections and local contacts, some set minimum stays, and associations may ban them. Always verify the city ordinance and any association rules for the specific property.
What extra costs come with short-term rentals?
Furnishing, cleaning, platform fees, management, utilities, and Florida and county tourist-development taxes on stays of six months or less.
How should I estimate income?
Use data on comparable nearby rentals across a full year, including the slower summer season, and compare it with a long-term rental scenario as a fallback.

faqs: What should I ask about an oceanfront condo building?
Ask for the milestone inspection and structural reports, reserve study and funding level, any current or planned special assessments, and the building's insurance cost.

Can I build or renovate on an oceanfront lot?
Work seaward of Florida's Coastal Construction Control Line needs a state permit in addition to local permits, so plan for extra review time.

segments.subhead: Annual-lease homes, townhomes and condos from $2,500 to $5,000 a month, updated every week.
intro: This search tracks homes, townhomes and condominiums available on an annual lease from $2,500 to $5,000 a month across Palm Beach, Broward and Miami-Dade.

Good rentals move fast, so it helps to have your documents ready and someone tracking new listings. Bill helps renters shortlist homes, arrange showings and handle applications, including association approvals where a condo or community requires one.
Each week the search is re-run, and this page shows the count and a link to every active listing.
faqs: What do I need to apply for a rental?
Typically a photo ID, proof of income, and consent to credit and background checks. Many condos and communities also require an association application and approval, which can take extra time.
Who pays the agent fee on a rental?
In most rentals the landlord pays the agent fee — we'll confirm before you sign.
How much move-in money should I plan for?
Commonly first month's rent, a security deposit, and sometimes last month's rent, plus any association application fee. Confirm the exact amounts for each listing.

segments.title: Seasonal Furnished Rentals: Palm Beach, Broward, Miami-Dade
segments.description: Furnished seasonal rentals in Palm Beach, Broward and Miami-Dade for winter visitors, monthly and multi-month stays. Active listings refreshed weekly.
segments.subhead: Furnished homes and condos for the winter season and other short stays, updated every week.
intro: This search tracks furnished homes and condominiums offered on monthly leases of one to eleven months across Palm Beach, Broward and Miami-Dade, the stays most winter visitors book between November and April.

The best seasonal rentals are often reserved months ahead, and condo associations may set minimum stays or limit how many times a unit can be leased each year. Bill helps visitors find furnished homes that fit their dates and checks the association rules before they commit.
Each week the search is re-run, and this page shows the count and a link to every active listing.
faqs: When should I book a winter rental?
As early as you can. Popular furnished homes for January through March are often reserved well ahead of the season.
Are there extra taxes on seasonal rentals?
Florida sales tax and county tourist-development tax generally apply to rentals of six months or less, and are usually added to the rent. Confirm the total with each listing.
Do condo associations restrict seasonal rentals?
Many do, with minimum lease lengths, a cap on leases per year, or an approval process. Bill checks the rules for each property before you book.
